item.title: Drua welcome new coaching team
item.description: THE Fijian Drua has added five experienced professionals to its coaching and performance structure as part of the Drua Vuvale for the upcoming 2027 season. Former Flying Fijians Ifereimi Rawaqa and Campese Ma’afu are among the additions, taking up the roles of forwards coach and scrum coach, respectively.
item.content:encoded:
THE Fijian Drua has added five experienced professionals to its coaching and performance structure as part of the Drua Vuvale for the upcoming 2027 season.

Former Flying Fijians Ifereimi Rawaqa and Campese Ma’afu are among the additions, taking up the roles of forwards coach and scrum coach, respectively.

Alando Soakai joins as defence coach, while Dr Dale Thomas has been appointed clinical and performance psychologist coach and Luke Vasu as head of athletic performance.

The appointments bring together different areas of expertise as the Drua continues to develop its high-performance environment.

Fiji Rugby Union chief executive Koli Sewabu welcomed the move, saying the appointments also reflected the importance of developing local coaching talent.

“On behalf of Fiji Rugby, I want to acknowledge the CEO Jeff Miller and the Drua for their commitment to our development systems,” Sewabu said.

“The appointments of Ifereimi Rawaqa and Campese Ma’afu showcase exactly what the Drua pathway was built for ­­-holistic growth.”

Rawaqa said being given the opportunity to work at professional level was both an honour and responsibility.

“As a local coach, it means a lot to have the opportunity to contribute to the Drua at this level. But I see it more as a responsibility than an achievement,” he said.

“There are a lot of talented local coaches coming through, and hopefully this opens the door and shows that there is a pathway for them too.”

Fiji Rugby Union general manager high-performance Naca Cawanibuka said Rawaqa and Ma’afu would bring their international playing experience into their new coaching roles.

He also highlighted Vasu’s development from a Fiji U20 trialist to a qualified sport science professional.

Vasu said he was grateful for the chance to return home and contribute to the franchise.

“I am truly excited and grateful for the opportunity to join the Drua vuvale,” he said.

Drua chief executive Jeff Miller said the coaching group would combine international expertise with a strong Fijian identity as the franchise enters its sixth season.

item.title: Navunikabi make winning start in badminton
item.description: THEY came to Suva as young athletes, but seven pupils from Navunikabi Primary School have already made their mark at the inaugural National Primary Schools Badminton Tournament. The Namosi youngsters won all their pool matches on Monday, the opening day of the three-day tournament at the FMF Gymnasium in Suva, and have progressed to the quarterfinals today.
item.content:encoded:
THEY came to Suva as young athletes, but seven pupils from Navunikabi Primary School have already made their mark at the inaugural National Primary Schools Badminton Tournament.

The Namosi youngsters won all their pool matches on Monday, the opening day of the three-day tournament at the FMF Gymnasium in Suva, and have progressed to the quarterfinals today.

Their success comes after a quick transition from athletics to badminton.

The pupils had originally been preparing for athletics, competing in their school’s inter-house competition before turning their attention to badminton.

Just a month later, they are competing at national level and have already secured a place in the knockout stages.

For principal Dan Kalouca, however, the results are only part of what the children are gaining from the experience.

“Experience in badminton,” Kalouca said when asked what he hoped the pupils would gain from the tournament.

The pupils had been training for about a month after their inter-house competition, with Kalouca saying the boys had embraced the challenge.

“They’ve been training for the past month and the boys are enjoying themselves,” he said.

Their unbeaten start on Monday has given the young side confidence heading into the knockout stages, but the tournament has also exposed them to a sporting environment beyond their usual surroundings.

For a school from Namosi, the trip to Suva has provided the pupils with an opportunity to compete against other primary schools while developing their understanding of a sport they are still relatively new to.

The school was also hoping to take the children to the Hibiscus Festival during their visit to Suva, giving them an opportunity to experience more of the capital outside the competition.

Navunikabi’s campaign is a reminder of how quickly young athletes can adapt when given an opportunity.

From preparing for athletics to taking up badminton and winning every pool match on their first day, the seven pupils have made an impressive start to their national campaign.

Today, however, brings a bigger challenge.

Navunikabi will be looking to win its quarterfinal and keep its unbeaten run alive, with a place in the semifinals and potentially the final later today at stake.

For seven pupils from Navunikabi Primary School, what began as a month-long shift from athletics to badminton could now take them all the way to the final on their first national stage.

item.title: Coates legacy
item.description: FOR the Vodafone Fijiana XV lock Jade Coates, wearing the Fiji jersey is about far more than rugby. It is a connection to family, heritage and a village thousands of kilometres away from where she was born and raised.
item.content:encoded:
FOR the Vodafone Fijiana XV lock Jade Coates, wearing the Fiji jersey is about far more than rugby.

It is a connection to family, heritage and a village thousands of kilometres away from where she was born and raised.

The 27-year-old New Zealand-born forward traces her Fijian roots to Nananu Village in Tailevu, where her grandmother is originally from.

Her father was also born and raised in Fiji before moving to New Zealand at the age of 14.

Now in her fifth year with the Fijiana XV, Coates says she remains grateful for every opportunity to represent the country of her family.

“I’m currently with the Fijiana XV for the fifth year now and, yeah, grateful to be here,” Coates said.

Her journey with Fiji has also been shaped by a strong family influence, particularly from her older sister, former Fijiana representative Brittany Coates.

As the youngest of four siblings, Jade says her sister played a significant role in opening the door for her own international rugby journey.

“My sister’s been a big part of my journey, so it’s been pretty cool that not only she was able to represent Fiji, but she opened that door for me to be able to,” she said.

The sisters remain close despite their busy lives, regularly speaking and sharing in each other’s journeys.

“Even now, we’re always on the phone every week, catching up, so it’s really cool and she’s really proud of me alongside the rest of my family.”

That family support continues to drive Coates as she prepares for another major chapter with the national side.

The Fijiana XV are currently building towards their Test against Japan before travelling on to Hong Kong for the WXV Global Series Challenger.

Coates says the squad has been putting in the hard work.

“We’re preparing well, the girls are working really hard,” she said.

As one of the more experienced members of a youthful Fijiana XV squad, Coates also recognises the responsibility she carries in helping the next generation find their feet in Test rugby.

The lock forward believes experience is most valuable when it is shared.

“If I can share my knowledge and skills to the girls, and they can share theirs to me, I think we’ll just be better off for it,” she said.

Coates is particularly proud of the young players coming through the squad, many of whom are still finding their confidence at international level.

“Really proud of the girls. We’ve got a young, youthful group here, very inexperienced in terms of Test rugby, so it’s just giving them the confidence that they deserve to be here.

“As a team, we’re very strong and powerful, and we can get the job done.”

From her family’s roots in Nananu Village to representing Fiji on the international stage, Coates continues to carry a legacy that began before she ever pulled on the white jersey.

And as the Fijiana XV prepare to take on new challenges in Japan and Hong Kong, she hopes Fiji’s supporters will continue to stand behind the team.

“Big thank you for everyone that’s supported us so far on our journey this year,” she said.

“Please tune in to watch us, especially on our tour now to Japan and Hong Kong.

“I know we’re playing miles away from home, but we definitely feel your support from far away, so we appreciate it.”

For Coates, the journey is one built on family, shared knowledge and pride in her Fijian heritage, and she is determined to continue making her family and Nananu Village proud.

item.title: Ellis in camp
item.description: A COACH who helped France reach two Rugby World Cup semi-finals and the 2011 final has been brought in to strengthen the FIJI Water Flying Fijians’ defence as Fiji begins a longer-term push towards next year’s World Cup. British coach David Ellis has been appointed interim Defence Coach by the Fiji Rugby Union (FRU) and is already in camp working with the players and national coaching staff.
item.content:encoded:
A COACH who helped France reach two Rugby World Cup semi-finals and the 2011 final has been brought in to strengthen the FIJI Water Flying Fijians’ defence as Fiji begins a longer-term push towards next year’s World Cup.

British coach David Ellis has been appointed interim Defence Coach by the Fiji Rugby Union (FRU) and is already in camp working with the players and national coaching staff.

Ellis served as France’s Assistant Coach for Defence from 2000 to 2011, helping Les Bleus reach the 2003 and 2007 World Cup semi-finals and the 2011 final, where they lost 7-8 to New Zealand.

France also won multiple Six Nations titles, including Grand Slams, during his tenure.

His immediate task is to strengthen Fiji’s defensive system, with FRU stating that his “immediate focus” will be “strengthening the team’s defensive systems and working with the wider coaching group”.

But the appointment is understood to form part of a broader strategy, with the Pacific Nations Cup providing Ellis’ first test before the Flying Fijians turn their attention to the Nations Championship later this year and, ultimately, the 2027 Rugby World Cup.

Ellis brings more than 25 years of coaching experience, including more than 1000 professional club matches and over 200 Test matches.

His international resume extends beyond France. He worked as a coaching consultant with the New Zealand All Blacks during their 3-0 British & Irish Lions series victory in 2005 and has held defence coaching roles with Tonga and Romania.

More recently, Ellis worked with Romania during its 2023 Rugby World Cup qualification campaign and helped the side secure bronze in the Rugby Europe Championship.

At club level, he has coached in England and France with Gloucester, Castres Olympique, CA Brive, London Irish and Lyon, helping Lyon to Pro D2 championship success in 2014 and 2016.

He has also served as a World Rugby Coach Development Mentor.

For Fiji, the Pacific Nations Cup is only the starting point.

The immediate goal is to build a more organised and resilient defence, but the bigger objective is to establish a defensive system capable of carrying the Flying Fijians through the Nations Championship and into the 2027 RWC.

item.title: Fiji creates history with sixth FANCA Premier title
item.description: THE Pacific Heavy Industries Fiji have written another memorable chapter in Fiji Muslim football history after being crowned Premier Champions of the Classic Buses FANCA Nations World Cup 2026 at Prince Charles Park. Fiji completed a remarkable tournament undefeated and without conceding a single goal, securing a historic sixth FANCA Premier title in front of a packed home crowd.
item.content:encoded:
THE Pacific Heavy Industries Fiji have written another memorable chapter in Fiji Muslim football history after being crowned Premier Champions of the Classic Buses FANCA Nations World Cup 2026 at Prince Charles Park.

Fiji completed a remarkable tournament undefeated and without conceding a single goal, securing a historic sixth FANCA Premier title in front of a packed home crowd.

Close to 4,000 supporters turned out at Prince Charles Park for the pulsating grand final, where Fiji defeated defending rivals New Zealand 1-0.

Ba striker Fazil Ali, popularly known as “Tiger”, proved to be the hero for the hosts after scoring the decisive goal in the opening minute of the match.

The early strike gave Fiji the perfect start, but they were made to work hard for the remainder of the contest as New Zealand pressed for an equaliser.

Fiji, however, showed tremendous courage, discipline and determination to protect their slender advantage until the final whistle.

The victory capped an extraordinary campaign for the home side, which finished the tournament undefeated while maintaining a perfect defensive record.

Zibraz Sahid was recognised for his outstanding performances throughout the competition after being named the tournament’s Most Valuable Player and Golden Ball winner.

Goalkeeper Mohammed Aziz also enjoyed a memorable campaign, claiming the Golden Glove award after helping Fiji complete the entire tournament without conceding a goal.

Fiji also received the Best Disciplined Nation award.

Fiji Head of Nation and FANCA 2026 Organising Committee chair Haji Javed Ahmed expressed immense pride in the team’s achievement, describing the victory as a fitting conclusion to a historic FANCA Nations World Cup on home soil.

The triumph carried additional significance as the tournament was staged alongside the Fiji Muslim League Centenary Celebrations, bringing together generations of the community through football, faith, brotherhood and unity.

Meanwhile, New Zealand defeated Fiji 2-1 to claim the Youth category title.

The United States of America edged hosts Fiji 5-4 in the Masters final, while New Zealand defeated Canada 1-0 to win the Legends category.

USA also claimed the Veterans title after defeating Fiji 3-0 in the final.

item.title: Young talent, big ambitions
item.description: FOR Ratu Tevita, Isireli, volleyball began as a childhood interest in Kinoya and has now grown into a dream of representing Fiji. The 14-year-old Year Nine student of Nasinu Secondary School was the most outstanding performer in the Under-17 grade at the Central Eastern Volleyball Championship on Friday, despite competing against older players.
item.content:encoded:
FOR Ratu Tevita, Isireli, volleyball began as a childhood interest in Kinoya and has now grown into a dream of representing Fiji.

The 14-year-old Year Nine student of Nasinu Secondary School was the most outstanding performer in the Under-17 grade at the Central Eastern Volleyball Championship on Friday, despite competing against older players.

Isireli, started playing volleyball in Year Five when he was just 10 years old.

Growing up in Kinoya, he quickly developed a passion for the sport and continued playing as he grew older.

Six years later, that early interest has developed into a promising sporting journey, with Isireli, now representing Nasinu Secondary School in the U17 grade.

His performance on Friday showed the progress he has made since first picking up a volleyball.

Isireli, is from Nakuruwai in Noco, Rewa, and has maternal links to Raviravi in Matuku, Lau.

While his family roots connect him to different parts of the country, Kinoya is where his love for volleyball began.

At Nasinu Secondary School, Isireli, has the opportunity to develop his skills while competing at a higher level against some of the country’s promising young players.

Being named the most outstanding performer has given him further motivation to continue working on his game.

For Isireli,, however, the recognition is only one step towards a bigger goal.

His ambition is to one day wear the Fiji colours and represent his country in volleyball.

That dream is now giving the young player something to work towards as he continues his development.

From a 10-year-old playing volleyball in Kinoya to becoming an U17 standout, Isireli,’s journey is still in its early stages.

With time on his side, the Nasinu student hopes Friday’s performance will be one of many milestones on his way to achieving his biggest goal — representing Fiji.

Ratu Tevita Isireli of Nasinu Secondary School sets the ball to his spikers against Gospel High School in the under-17 boys finals during the Central Eastern Secondary Schools Volleyball Championship at the National Netball Centre in Suva on Friday, August 28, 2026. Picture: JONACANI LALAKOBAU

item.title: Turagaluvu finds his feet on the badminton court
item.description: SAKARAIA Turagaluvu may be new to badminton, but the Veiuto Primary School Year Seven student is quickly discovering the competitive side of the sport. Competing at the inaugural National Primary Schools Badminton Tournament at the FMF Gymnasium in Suva, Turagaluvu is embracing the challenge of testing himself against other young shuttlers from around the country.
item.content:encoded:
SAKARAIA Turagaluvu may be new to badminton, but the Veiuto Primary School Year Seven student is quickly discovering the competitive side of the sport.

Competing at the inaugural National Primary Schools Badminton Tournament at the FMF Gymnasium in Suva, Turagaluvu is embracing the challenge of testing himself against other young shuttlers from around the country.

His tournament did not begin as planned after he lost his opening match on Monday, but the setback did little to dent his confidence.

“Yesterday (Monday), I lost my first game, but I won all. Today (yesterday), I have been winning my games. I hope to win more matches,” he said.

The youngster has since found his rhythm on the court, turning his early disappointment into motivation as he continues to learn and improve with every match.

For Turagaluvu, the tournament is not only about winning but also enjoying the opportunity to compete at a national level.

Asked whether he believed he could continue his winning run, he was quick to respond.

His confidence will be put to the test today when the tournament moves into the quarterfinals, with Turagaluvu hoping to book his place in the next stage.

The experience has also given him a taste of the discipline required in badminton, with training sessions helping him prepare for the intensity of competition.

“Training was good. They are all so strict,” he said.

Despite being new to the sport, Turagaluvu has already shown the attitude needed to compete, bouncing back from his first-match defeat and building momentum as the tournament progressed.

With the quarterfinals underway today, he will be aiming to maintain that momentum and continue his run in the historic first National Primary Schools Badminton Tournament.

For the Veiuto youngster, every match presents another opportunity to learn, compete and prove himself on the court.

And while the pressure increases as the tournament reaches its knockout stages, Turagaluvu remains confident in his ability to rise to the challenge.

“I want to thank the Lord and thank my parents for supporting me,” he said.

item.title: Two sisters, one dream
item.description: TORIKA Boseiwaqa is following the trail blazed by elder sister Sereana as the 14-year-old begins her own Kulas journey with a World Cup qualification target in sight. For the Boseiwaqa sisters, the Fiji jersey is no longer just a dream watched from the sidelines — it is a family tradition taking shape before their eyes.
item.content:encoded:
TORIKA Boseiwaqa is following the trail blazed by elder sister Sereana as the 14-year-old begins her own Kulas journey with a World Cup qualification target in sight.

For the Boseiwaqa sisters, the Fiji jersey is no longer just a dream watched from the sidelines — it is a family tradition taking shape before their eyes.

Fourteen-year-old Torika Boseiwaqa has earned her first national call-up after being selected for the Fiji Mini Kulas squad for the OFC U-16 Women’s Championship in Solomon Islands.

The year nine student of Ba Sangam College is the youngest of five siblings and has spent years watching elder sister Sereana Naweni rise through Fiji’s age-group ranks before establishing herself with the senior Kulas.

Naweni captained Fiji at the 2025 OFC U-19 Women’s Championship and scored for the senior side against Tonga at last year’s OFC Women’s Nations Cup.

Now Torika has her own opportunity to follow that path.

“My elder sister has supported me a lot and always encourages me to work hard,” Torika said.

“I am very proud to follow in her footsteps and represent Fiji, just like she has done.”

Her challenge is bigger than simply making her international debut.

The Mini Kulas will face the Cook Islands on September 6, New Zealand on September 9 and hosts Solomon Islands on September 12, with the two finalists qualifying for the FIFA U-17 Women’s World Cup 2027.

That gives Torika and her teammates a clear target — finish among the top two in Oceania and take Fiji to the world stage.

Torika knows the opportunity comes with responsibility.

“She has inspired me, and I hope to make her and my family proud when I play for the Mini Kulas,” she said.

For the Boseiwaqa family, it is already a remarkable milestone.

Sereana has shown Torika what is possible in the Fiji jersey.

Now the younger sister has the chance to write her own chapter — while chasing a dream that could take her first international tournament all the way to a World Cup.
